nodes.label: ULK1 (at Ser757)
nodes.description: Under nutrient-rich conditions, mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757, disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction and suppressing autophagy.

nodes.label: ULK1
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates ULK1 at multiple lysine residues, promoting its kinase activity and autophagy initiation under glucose starvation.

nodes.label: STRAD and MO25 for activity
nodes.description: Without STRAD and MO25 binding, LKB1 remains in the nucleus and exhibits minimal kinase activity.

nodes.label: Thr172
nodes.description: LKB1 is the primary upstream kinase that phosphorylates AMPK at Thr172 within the activation loop, increasing AMPK activity >100-fold.

nodes.label: LKB1 deficiency
nodes.description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk.

nodes.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome

nodes.label: Beclin1 BH3 domain
nodes.description: Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL bind the BH3 domain of Beclin1, sequestering it and inhibiting autophagy.

nodes.label: Bcl-2 anti-apoptotic proteins
nodes.description: Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL bind the BH3 domain of Beclin1, sequestering it and inhibiting autophagy.

nodes.label: Four distinct class III PI3K complexes
nodes.description: Beclin1 assembles Complex I (Atg14L), II (UVRAG), III (UVRAG+Rubicon), and IV (Bif-1) to regulate autophagy at different stages.

nodes.label: Tumour suppressor (glutamine metabolism)
nodes.description: SIRT4 inhibits GDH activity, restricting anaplerotic carbon supply to the TCA cycle in cancer cells, suppressing tumour growth.

nodes.label: MTPα (fatty acid oxidation)
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty acid oxidation in the liver by inhibiting mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα).

nodes.label: H3K18ac
nodes.description: SIRT7 possesses NAD+-dependent deacetylase activity with high selectivity for histone H3 at lysine 18 (H3K18ac), a repressive mark.

nodes.label: Replicative lifespan
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction.

nodes.label: 1.5 to 3 mg per liter
nodes.description: Typical red wine contains 1.5 to 3 mg/L trans-resveratrol; high-altitude Malbecs or cool-climate Pinot Noirs can reach up to 5.8 mg/L. A standard 5-ounce glass contains ~0.3 mg.

nodes.label: 0.15 to 1.3 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Raw red grapes contain roughly 0.15 to 1.3 mg resveratrol per 100 grams, mostly concentrated in the skins.

nodes.label: Vine Tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata)
nodes.description: Vine tea (Rattan Tea) dry leaves contain 20% to 30% DHM by weight, making 1-1.5g of dry leaves sufficient for a 300mg therapeutic dose.

nodes.label: Cyanidin-3-glucoside
nodes.description: Black elderberries contain roughly 350 to 450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100g fresh berries; 70-85g (~1 cup) reaches the 300mg therapeutic threshold.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.description: Honokiol is highly lipophilic with extremely poor water solubility. Traditional hot-water tea extraction is inefficient; ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are required for therapeutic dosing.

nodes.label: Dual mechanism (direct + indirect)
nodes.description: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 through direct allosteric binding at the NTD (Glu230) AND indirect activation via the PDE4/cAMP/Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT/NAD+ axis.
